spatial_claims.claim: Vertices A, B, C, D, E in cyclic boundary order forming a convex equilateral pentagon; case split into consecutive (B,C,D) and nonconsecutive (A,B,D) equal angles
SAS on triangles ABC and EDC: sides AB=ED, BC=DC with included angles B=D, yielding AC=EC and angle BAC = angle DEC
Angle decomposition at A: angle BAE = angle BAC + angle CAE, requiring ray AC between rays AB and AE
Angle decomposition at E: angle DEA = angle DEC + angle CEA, requiring ray EC between rays ED and EA
SAS on triangles ABC and BCD: sides AB=BC, BC=CD with included angles B=C, yielding AC=BD
SSS on triangles BAD and CDA: BA=CD, BD=CA, AD common, yielding angle BAD = angle CDA
Isosceles triangle ADE with AE=DE, so angle DAE = angle ADE
Angle decomposition at A: angle BAE = angle BAD + angle DAE, requiring ray AD between rays AB and AE
Angle decomposition at D: angle CDE = angle CDA + angle ADE, requiring ray DA between rays DC and DE
Cyclic relabeling of nonconsecutive case (A,B,D equal with E=A derived) to consecutive case (E,A,B are three consecutive equal angles)

configuration_map: Convex equilateral pentagon ABCDE with vertices in cyclic order. From vertex A, rays to other vertices through the interior are ordered: AB, AC, AD, AE. From vertex E, the order is: ED, EC, EB, EA. From vertex D, the order is: DC, DB, DA, DE. All diagonals (AC, CE, BD, AD) lie in the pentagon's interior. Ray AC is between rays AB and AE at vertex A. Ray EC is between rays ED and EA at vertex E. Ray AD is between rays AB and AE at vertex A (closer to AE than AC). Ray DA is between rays DC and DE at vertex D. All angle decompositions in Steps 3 and 6 are consistent with these ray orderings.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. Every angle decomposition (Steps 3 and 6) has the middle ray correctly positioned between the outer rays in the convex pentagon. All SAS and SSS triangle congruence applications use valid side-angle correspondences. The case analysis is complete: in a 5-cycle, the maximum independent set has size 2, so any 3 vertices include an adjacent pair, and under cyclic relabeling all non-consecutive triples reduce to {A,B,D}. The nonconsecutive-to-consecutive reduction in Step 7 is valid.
